analysis:
The Chief Minister's Free Medicine Scheme (Mukhyamantri Nishulk Dava Yojana) was launched in Rajasthan on 2 October 2011, offering essential medicines free of cost at government health facilities. At the launch at Dausa, Chief Minister Ashok Gehlot said the scheme began with 200 medicines and would be raised to 400 by January.

The state later reported to the Rajasthan Assembly that free-medicine beneficiaries numbered 52.4 crore between 2 October 2011 and December 2017, while free diagnostic tests were added from 2013. The number of free medicines was subsequently raised to 608 and then 712.

The scheme carried over across changes of government. A Ministry of Health and Family Welfare assessment placed Rajasthan first among 16 states on implementation of free-medicine schemes.
notes: The 400-medicines-by-January promise was delivered and exceeded, so the verdict is true. Beneficiary counts are cumulative visits, not unique individuals, as the Indian Express report notes.
